title: Collective dynamics of harmonically trapped 1D quantum droplets under linear gravitational-like confinement
authors: Saurab Das, Jayanta Bera, Ajay Nath
abstract: We investigate the dynamics of harmonically confined quantum droplets in a binary Bose Einstein condensate within the one dimensional extended Gross Pitaevskii framework, including LHY corrections, under a constant linear (gravitational like) potential. By analyzing the COM and width dynamics, we show that the monopole (breathing) mode remains governed by the harmonic confinement, with a frequency asymptotically insensitive to the linear perturbation, demonstrating the robustness of internal collective excitations against uniform external forcing. In contrast, the COM exhibits interaction-dependent transport, with weak confinement producing large susceptibility and rapid displacement, whereas strong confinement suppresses transport even under large forcing. The COM response decreases monotonically with increasing trap frequency. We further characterize the evolving quantum state through the quantum Fisher information and Wigner quasi-probability distributions, showing that the linear potential enables controlled generation of states with enhanced metrological sensitivity over finite times, while stronger confinement shifts the onset of the high-sensitivity regime to larger forcing strengths. Numerical simulations based on the split-step Fourier method confirm the dynamical stability of the obtained solutions. These results illustrate the impact of linear gravitational like trap on the collective excitations, transport, and quantum metrological properties of 1D ultradilute quantum fluids.
summary: The paper analyzes the collective dynamics of 1D quantum droplets confined by both harmonic and linear trapping potentials. It demonstrates that while the breathing mode is robust against the linear force, the center-of-mass motion is highly sensitive to confinement strength. Crucially, it shows that this controlled external forcing can be utilized to generate quantum states with enhanced sensitivity for metrology applications.
main_problem: Investigating the collective dynamics, transport properties, and quantum metrological potential of harmonically trapped 1D quantum droplets under a linear gravitational-like confinement.
main_result: The breathing mode remains robust against linear forcing, while the center-of-mass (COM) motion exhibits strong dependence on trap strength; furthermore, the linear potential enables controlled generation of states with enhanced metrological sensitivity.
method: Analytical treatment using ansatz solutions for the extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation (eGPE), supplemented by numerical simulations via the split-step Fourier method and analysis using Quantum Fisher Information (QFI).
model_or_system: The system models a binary Bose-Einstein condensate forming quantum droplets in one dimension, governed by the 1D eGPE which incorporates Lee-Huang-Yang (LHY) corrections. The confinement potential is a combination of harmonic trapping and a linear gravitational-like term.
key_observables: Center-of-mass (COM) dynamics, breathing mode frequency, Quantum Fisher Information (QFI), and Wigner quasi-probability distributions.
important_parameters: Harmonic trap strength ($M$), linear potential strength ($a$), interaction coefficients ($\delta g(t)$, $g_1(t)$).
main_assumptions: The system is effectively one-dimensional (assuming $\omega_x \ll \omega_\perp$). The analysis relies on specific ansatz solutions for the wavefunction.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the time evolution of QFI showing revival patterns, Wigner distributions showing phase-space changes due to confinement parameters ($a$ and $M$), and density profiles confirming dynamical stability under noise.
paper_structure: The paper analyzes the dynamics by first establishing the governing eGPE with LHY corrections. It then examines the COM transport vs. trap strength, contrasts this with the robust breathing mode, and finally uses QFI and Wigner functions to characterize how linear forcing controls quantum metrological sensitivity.
why_interesting: This work bridges fundamental many-body physics (quantum droplets) with applied topics like quantum sensing, showing how external potentials can be tuned to enhance measurement precision while maintaining stability in internal excitations.
